All changes are in place and verified. Here's a summary of what I did and why.

## Changes

next.config.ts — enabled partialPrefetching: true. This is required for the prefetch() stage function to take effect (it needs both cacheComponents and partialPrefetching). It switches <Link> to the three-stage model: App Shell → per-link prefetch → navigation.

app/product/page.tsx — split the related products into a separate async RelatedProducts component wrapped in <Suspense>, with await prefetch() above the getRelatedProducts() call. The product heading and description stay above the boundary, so they remain in the App Shell. await prefetch() keeps everything below it out of the App Shell, deferring it to a per-link prefetch or the navigation. The cached data (cacheLife('hours')) keeps its lifetime because the use cache directive stays on getRelatedProducts, called below prefetch().

app/page.tsx — set prefetch={true} on the featured-product <Link>. A bare <Link> only prefetches the App Shell (no related products). A prefetch={true} link triggers a per-link prefetch, which resolves the content below prefetch() ahead of the click — so related products are ready immediately when navigating from that link.

## How it satisfies the request

- Default prefetch (any bare <Link> to /product): fetches only the App Shell — the heading, description, and the "Loading related products..." Suspense fallback. Related products are excluded.
- Featured-product link (prefetch={true}): triggers a per-link prefetch that resolves the related products before the click, so they're ready immediately on navigation.
- Direct visit / full navigation: prefetch() has no effect on the initial load, so the full page (including related products) renders normally.

## Verification

- npm run build — exit code 0. Output confirmed "Cache Components enabled" and "Partial Prefetching enabled"; TypeScript passed; /product route shows 1h revalidate / 1d expire matching cacheLife('hours').
- Production server (next start) — / returned 200 with the featured-product link; /product rendered the heading, the Suspense fallback, and both related-product list items.

One note: next build auto-updated tsconfig.json (set jsx to react-jsx and added .next/dev/types//.ts to include). That's a standard Next.js-managed change, not something I edited.
